newsitem.title: USA: Calif. Senate convenes special session on floods.
newsitem.headline: Calif. Senate convenes special session on floods.

text.p: California's state Senate on Friday convened in a special session called to consider measures to aid the victims of recent flooding and help counties cope with the damage.
No new legislation was introduced during Friday's brief session, but officials said it would reconvene next week.
The state Assembly met in special session on Tuesday.

Several state lawmakers said they planned to introduce proposals to aid victims of the floods and hard-hit local governments. A special session waives certain rules, allowing the legislature to act more quickly on relief proposals.

Earlier this week, measures were introduced to make $170 million available to the Department of Water Resources, to provide property and income tax relief for flood victims, and to help to reimburse county losses.
Damage estimates from the devastating New Year floods have passed $1.5 billion. Nearly 16,000 homes have been damaged or destroyed in the flooding, according to state figures.
State officials said the floods were almost certain to be the most costly in state history, surpassing the $1.8 billion of losses suffered in severe 1995 floods.
